issues.failure_explanation: MFCQ constrains only active-constraint multipliers through the partial x-Jacobian system (eq:22122025b). The joint system (eq:mfcqduo) also involves inactive-constraint multipliers that are unconstrained in sign. Counterexample: n=1, q=1, m=2, no equality constraints, g₁ = −x+1, g₂ = x at (0,0). Here I = {2}, MFCQ holds (direction d = −1 works). Jac G(0,0)ᵀλ = (−λ₁+λ₂, 0)ᵀ, so λ₁ = λ₂ = 1 satisfies the joint equation with λ₂ ≥ 0 but λ₂ = 1 ≠ 0, contradicting the stated conclusion. The claim holds only after adding the constraint λᵢ = 0 for inactive i (which the normal cone in the chain-rule application does supply).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the constraint λᵢ = 0 for all i ∉ I(x,θ) (equivalently, λᵢ gᵢ(x,θ) = 0) to the hypothesis of eq:mfcqduo. With this addition, the x-block of the joint equation reduces to the dual MFCQ system and the conclusion follows.
issues.overall_effect: The remark's stated implication is false as written. Its use in Section sect:parametricOptimality to justify the chain-rule application is imprecise, though the correct restricted version (with inactive multipliers zeroed) does hold and suffices for that application. Proposition prop:locboundp's proof correctly invokes eq:22122025b on the x-block after complementarity zeroes inactive multipliers, so it is unaffected.
issues.title: Joint dual MFCQ implication is false
issues.why_classification: A short local correction (adding complementarity for inactive multipliers) makes the statement true and preserves every downstream claim, since the only application already implicitly uses the corrected version via the normal cone.

issues.failure_explanation: The KKT stationarity gives Jac_x Gᵀλₖ + Jac_x Hᵀμₖ = −vₖ. Dividing by ‖(λₖ,μₖ)‖ yields Jac_x Gᵀαₖ + Jac_x Hᵀβₖ = −vₖ/‖(λₖ,μₖ)‖, where ‖(λₖ,μₖ)‖ → ∞ makes the right-hand side vanish. The proof instead writes the denominator as ‖(αₖ,βₖ)‖ = 1, making the right-hand side equal to −vₖ (bounded but not vanishing). Taking the limit of the proof's equation gives Jac_x Gᵀα + Jac_x Hᵀβ = −v, which need not be zero; the claimed limit of zero (eq:21122025a) does not follow. The correct denominator ‖(λₖ,μₖ)‖ restores the vanishing right-hand side and the correct limit.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ‖(αₖ,βₖ)‖ with ‖(λₖ,μₖ)‖ in the denominator of eq:22122025a. The boundedness of vₖ then makes the right-hand side converge to zero, giving eq:21122025a correctly.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate equation eq:22122025a is wrong, and the inference to eq:21122025a is unjustified as written. However, correcting the denominator makes the proof valid and the conclusion of Proposition prop:locboundp (local boundedness of Sol_pd) is unaffected. Downstream results that invoke prop:locboundp remain valid once this is fixed.
issues.title: Normalization error in local boundedness proof of primal-dual solution map
issues.why_classification: A single-symbol correction in one displayed equation restores the correct inference. The conclusion and all downstream results survive unchanged with no new argument needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem defines D_f(θ) using conv D_F(x,θ) in the set-membership condition (0,u) ∈ conv D_F(x,θ) + (constraint terms). The proof, however, defines D_L using D_F (without conv) and establishes the chain rule for D_L. The KKT stationarity condition (via Mult) guarantees the existence of an element with zero x-component only in conv D_F(x,θ) + (constraint terms), not in D_F(x,θ) + (constraint terms). When D_F(x,θ) is non-convex, the set {(v,u) ∈ D_L(y,θ) : v = 0} may be empty, making the chain-rule conclusion for the θ-component vacuous. Lemma lem:edlem9, invoked in the final step, is stated in terms of conv D_F, creating a mismatch with the D_F-based chain rule. The chain rule does extend from D_F to conv D_F by linearity of the inner product, but this extension is not made.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace D_F with conv D_F in the definition of D_L and extend the chain rule from D_F to conv D_F by linearity (the inner-product expression ⟨ẋ,z⟩+⟨θ̇,w⟩ is affine in (z,w), so if it is constant on D_F it is constant on conv D_F). Reapply Lemma lem:edlem8 to conv D_L, then Lemma lem:edlem9 as stated. All other arguments remain unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem theo:main establishes the chain rule only for elements of D_F(x,θ) + constraints, not for the larger set conv D_F(x,θ) + constraints used in the definition of D_f. As a result, conservativity of D_f as defined in the theorem is not fully proved. Theorem theo:mainsmooth (the smooth special case where D_F is a singleton) is unaffected since conv D_F = D_F there.
issues.title: Main theorem proof uses D_F where conv D_F is required
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a contained but nontrivial modification: changing the definition of D_L throughout the proof, extending the chain rule to convex hulls, and rechecking the definability and compact-valuedness of conv D_L. No new global proof architecture is needed and no claim is lost, but the gap goes beyond routine algebra.

issues.failure_explanation: The construction ḡ(z) = f̄(z) + Σₖ φ(‖z−zₖ‖/rₖ)rₖ is differentiable at points z̄ ∈ C only if the bump radii satisfy rₖ = o(dist(zₖ,C)) as zₖ → z̄. The stated constraints on rₖ (positive, vanishing, pairwise disjoint supports) do not impose this. For example, with rₖ = dist(zₖ,C)/2 the difference quotient ḡ(z̄+h)/‖h‖ evaluated at h = zₖ−z̄ equals φ(0)·rₖ/‖zₖ−z̄‖ = φ(0)/2, which does not vanish, so the Fréchet derivative does not exist at z̄. The proof asserts differentiability without verifying it for the stated constraints on rₖ. Choosing rₖ = dist(zₖ,C)² does yield differentiability (with gradient 0 on C) while preserving the Clarke-subdifferential inclusion B_c(0,1) ⊂ ∂ᶜ ḡ(z), but this choice is not made or justified.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the choice of radii to rₖ = o(dist(zₖ,C)) (e.g. rₖ = dist(zₖ,C)²) and verify that ḡ(z̄+h) = o(‖h‖) at every z̄ ∈ C. The φ-term contribution is bounded by max|φ|·rₖ = o(dist(zₖ,C)) = o(‖h‖) whenever z̄+h lies in some B(zₖ,rₖ), and the f̄-term is O(‖h‖²). The Clarke-subdifferential inclusion B_c(0,1) ⊂ ∂ᶜ ḡ(z) is preserved since the gradient-limit argument at points zₖ − (rₖ/2)v is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Claim lem:fnctcounterex's promise of a differentiable function is unproved for the stated construction. Claim theo:counterex inherits this gap in its assertion (ii) that F is differentiable on ℝ², weakening the advertised result that 'even differentiability of F is not sufficient' to the weaker statement that local Lipschitz continuity and path differentiability are not sufficient. The core conclusion of theo:counterex (D_f is not conservative) is independently established and is unaffected.
issues.title: Counterexample function claimed differentiable but differentiability not established
issues.why_classification: Establishing the claimed differentiability requires a specific (non-arbitrary) choice of the radii rₖ together with a contained nontrivial verification of Fréchet differentiability at every point of C. Without this, a substantive advertised property (differentiability of the counterexample objective) is unsupported, weakening theo:counterex's stated scope. The repair preserves all claims but goes beyond a routine local edit.
